banner_warn_write: ⚠ Current permission is write: terminal_exec can run arbitrary shell commands. Start with readonly in production and switch via /permission when needed.
banner_hint: Type {help} for commands, {at} for shortcuts, {exit} to quit
banner_missing_key: ⚠ No API key configured yet — choose 2 (Setup wizard) for first-time login
banner_nav: ↑/↓ select · number to jump · Enter confirm · Esc/q quit
menu_more: … {n} more (keep typing to narrow it down)
menu_hint_command: ↑↓ select · Tab complete · Enter sends (a fully typed command runs on one Enter) · Esc closes
menu_hint_arg: ↑↓ pick an argument · Tab complete · Enter sends · Esc closes
menu_hint_mention: ↑↓ select · Tab complete · @file/@folder accept paths · Esc closes
search_hint: reverse history search: keep typing to filter · Enter accepts · Esc cancels
auto_reject_plan: Non-interactive mode: plan auto-rejected (no approver present).
perm_request_title: Agent requests temporary access to tool: {tool}
perm_approve_q: Grant access? [y once / a this session / N deny]:
perm_granted_session_msg: Granted for this session; won't ask again for this tool.
perm_session_refused: {tool} cannot be granted session-wide (dangerous commands and outbound destinations need per-call review); treated as one-time.
security_alert: ⚠ {n} execution-layer security blocks in this session (latest: {tool}).
security_alert_hint: If this wasn't your request, something read from a file/web page may be injecting instructions — stop and check the sources, or end this session (/exit).
unattended_notice: ⚠ Unattended + no kernel boundary (non-TTY stdin, sandbox off, not read-only): actions that need approval are REJECTED outright (terminal_exec is unusable in CI), while write/execute tools that need no approval (file_write / code_execute / api_post …) run under in-process policy only. For unattended runs pass --sandbox job/docker (optionally --approval-policy on_failure), or go back to --permission readonly.
sandbox_preflight_job_non_windows: ⚠ --sandbox job is a Windows-only Job Object primitive and cannot work on this platform: startup is not blocked, but the first terminal_exec / code_execute will honestly return 503 (it never falls back to the host). On Linux/macOS use --sandbox docker (one-shot container), or accept the in-process policy layer of the off tier.
sandbox_preflight_job_no_executor: ⚠ --sandbox job needs the Go executor but its binary was not found: the first call will return 503. Run `ace --install-executor` (official prebuilt, no local Go needed), or `cd executor && go build -o ace-executor(.exe) .`.
sandbox_preflight_docker_no_cli: ⚠ --sandbox docker needs the Docker CLI, and `docker` is not on PATH: the first call will return 503 (no fallback to the host). Install/start Docker and retry, or stay on the off tier (in-process policy only).
policy_refused_never_without_boundary: ❌ Refusing to start: approval_policy=never (never ask) + sandbox=off (no kernel boundary). `never` does not add dangerous actions (anything needing approval is denied), but it does not stop the tools that need no approval (file_write / code_execute / api_post …) — no human plus no boundary means no boundary. For unattended runs give a real boundary: --sandbox job or --sandbox docker (optionally with --approval-policy on_failure for try-then-ask).
policy_refused_never_with_danger_full_ac: ❌ Refusing to start: approval_policy=never + sandbox_policy=danger_full_access. ADR-002 states this combination has no legitimate use (unattended with no isolation). Use workspace_write / read_only, or give a real boundary with --sandbox job|docker.
max_rounds: ⚠ Reached max rounds, Agent did not give a final reply.
unverified_claim: ⚠ The model claimed the action was done, but no tool ran this round — nothing actually happened. Asked it to call a tool for real.
unverified_claim_final: ⚠ The "done" above is fabricated: no tool was executed in this turn and nothing on disk changed. Use a larger tool-calling model, or verify with /status.
help_hint: Tip: type @ for shortcuts (@lang switch language / @skill switch skill / @file reference file / @folder reference folder)
unknown_prefix: No command starts with '{name}' (type / to see all)
cmd_help: Show help (type / or any prefix for suggestions)
cmd_undo: Roll back to the latest auto snapshot (no id needed)
cmd_rollback: Roll back to a snapshot (usage: /rollback <snapshot id>)
cmd_permission: Switch permission (Enter shows picker), or /permission [readonly|write|full] · /permission rules edits session-level rules
rules_hint: Checked = never ask again this session; unchecking revokes immediately
rules_none: Nothing needs authorising at this level — /permission rules is for tools that still ask.
rules_non_tty: Non-interactive session: rules are listed, nothing is changed.
rules_single_only: These cannot be granted for the session ({n}), they stay per-call: {tools}
wizard_help_provider: Switches base_url and picks that provider's default model
wizard_bad_provider: Enter a number between 1 and {n} (empty = keep current)
wizard_help_model: Choices follow the provider chosen above
wizard_cancelled: Cancelled — nothing was changed or saved.
cmd_mock: Toggle offline demo / real model (switch back and forth)
cmd_open: Open file with system default app (usage: /open <path>)
cmd_edit: Open file with VS Code (or default editor) (usage: /edit <path>)
at_skill_usage: Usage: @skill coding | writing | analysis | fiction | general
at_file_usage: Usage: @file <path> (relative to project dir or absolute, e.g. @file README.md)
at_file_is_dir: This is a folder; use @folder or specify a file.
skill_coding_desc: Focus on writing, fixing, debugging and explaining code
skill_writing_desc: Focus on writing, polishing, summarizing and reports
skill_analysis_desc: Focus on data analysis, statistics and reports
skill_fiction_desc: Focus on novels, stories, characters and plots
undo_none: No snapshot to roll back (a snapshot is auto-created before each write)
stall_abort: WARNING: Agent failed/blocked for {n} consecutive rounds and was auto-aborted. Please rephrase your request or check the model.
compact_done: ⓘ Context compacted: {before} → {after} tokens (earlier turns folded into a summary)
compact_failed: ⚠ Context compaction errored, skipped this turn: {err}
cmd_goal: View/manage the persistent goal (usage: /goal [resume|pause|complete|status]); long tasks auto-continue round by round
cmd_audit: View session event log (full-chain audit; usage: /audit [count] [kind])
model_err_401: API Key invalid or expired. Reconfigure it via /config (GLM keys start with 'id.'; no spaces/newlines), or regenerate one in the provider console.
model_err_403: Key lacks permission for this model: check account/quota, or switch model.
model_err_404: Endpoint or model not found: check base_url and model name (e.g. glm-4-flash / deepseek-chat).
model_err_429: Rate limited or quota exhausted: retry later, or check your balance.
banner_sandbox_off: Sandbox: off (Python-level policy checks, no kernel boundary)
goal_no_goal: No active goal. Create one with goal_create (or just ask the agent).
goal_no_active: No active goal (create via goal_create or ask the agent).
trunc_hint: truncated {cut} chars, original {total}; use file_read for the full content
session_resumed: Resumed previous session ({n} messages, {file}); /clear to reset
goal_pending: Unfinished goal ({phase}): {obj}  /goal to view or resume
subagent_no_approval: No human approval is available in the subagent environment. Stop using plan_propose / request_permission; use a way that needs no approval, or give a conclusion directly.
subagent_limit: (subagent hit the 8-round limit without a conclusion)
cmd_sandbox: Switch execution sandbox tier (Enter shows picker, or /sandbox [off|job|docker])
cmd_net: Toggle networking (Enter shows picker, or /net on|off to set explicitly)
net_status: Network: {state} (online tools like search/api_get/browser follow the switch)
sandbox_set: Sandbox tier switched to: {mode} (session/history/permissions kept; only future terminal_exec / code_execute are affected)
sandbox_usage: Usage: /sandbox pick via Enter, or /sandbox off|job|docker (off=host, job=Job Object boundary, docker=one-shot container)
cmd_expand: Expand the last folded tool output (what the card's "expand to see it all" refers to)
expand_none: Nothing to expand — only tool output that was folded can be expanded (the card says "N lines folded").
cmd_diff: Change log: which files changed first, then the line-by-line diff of one entry (/diff [n])
cmd_statusline: Which segments the status line shows and in what order (/statusline model,context,-turns)
cmd_tasks: Draw the goal, the checklist and the running tool as one multi-line task tree
cmd_fullscreen: Toggle the alternate-screen session (fixed header/scroll area/status line; F5 leaves it)
fullscreen_on: Full-screen session: on (applies next time chat starts; F5 leaves it)
fullscreen_off: Full-screen session: off (back to the plain line-by-line REPL)
fullscreen_next_turn: In full screen: PageUp/↑ scrolls back · End returns to the bottom · Ctrl+O expands the last folded output
fullscreen_hint: Full-screen session ready. Type to chat; PageUp/↑ scrolls back, End returns to the bottom, F5 leaves full screen.
fullscreen_off_hint: Left full screen, back to the plain REPL (/fullscreen on to re-enter).
statusline_hint: /statusline model,context,-turns reorders; -name removes a segment (narrow terminals drop decoration by priority)
statusline_save_failed: Applied in this session, but the config could not be written (next start returns to the default order)
tasks_none: No goal and no checklist — create one with goal_create / todo_write, or look at /goal and /todo.
ctx_meter: Context {bar} {pct}% (an estimate, not a server reading)
diff_none: No changes recorded yet — only write-type tools that produce a diff show up here.
diff_hint: /diff <n> for the full diff · /review turns the newest entry into a patch you edit
status_context: Context: ~{tokens} tokens / window {window} ({pct}%, compaction triggers near {trigger}; an estimate, not a server reading)
status_context_nocompact: ↳ --no-compact is on: past the window, history is hard-truncated (early turns are simply dropped)
ctx_warn_near: ⚠ Context is an estimated {pct}% full (~{tokens} tokens, trigger {trigger}) — getting close. Stay on the topic if you want it, or /clear for a fresh one.
ctx_warn_over: ⚠ Context is an estimated {pct}% full (~{tokens} tokens, trigger {trigger}) — the next round folds the middle into a summary: recent turns stay verbatim, the middle is compacted (the originals stay in the session log).
banner_tagline: A local AI coding agent · safety lives in the execution layer, not the prompt
preview_hint: This is a UI preview (--preview draws the screen and exits). In a real run: ↑/↓ to move · digits to jump · Enter to confirm · Esc/q to quit.
preview_footer_title: Status bar (live in a real session)
history_empty: No history yet (cross-session history lives in ~/.ace_history; ACE_NO_HISTORY=1 keeps it in memory)
history_recent: Last {n} inputs (↑/↓ or Ctrl+R also work):
history_pick: Pick a past input (Enter fills the prompt, it is not sent)
history_hint: Picked entries fill the next prompt (never auto-sent) · Ctrl+R searches backwards
input_hint_multiline: Multiline: Alt+Enter or Ctrl+J inserts a newline (Shift+Enter depends on the terminal); Enter sends
input_hint_history: History search: Ctrl+R backwards · /history fuzzy search (dsk finds deepseek)
cmd_mcp: MCP server status and tool list (external process tools)
mcp_config_hint: Configure with "mcp_servers": {"name": {"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/tmp"]}} in ~/.ai_code.json, or a project-level .ace/mcp.json (project wins on name clashes).
mcp_footer: Note: an MCP server is a child process you configured and is **not inside ACE's sandbox** — only add servers you trust. /mcp notools shows status only.
cmd_hooks: Show event hooks (your own checks) and their last results
cmd_plugins: Show loaded plugins and what they contribute
hooks_config_hint: Configure with "hooks": {"pre_tool": ["python .ace/hooks/check.py"], "post_tool": [...]} in ~/.ai_code.json, or a project-level .ace/hooks.json; plugin hooks.json files are appended too. A hook reads JSON on stdin and answers {"decision":"allow|block","reason":"..."} on stdout; exit code 2 blocks.
hooks_footer: Hooks are **local commands you configured and are not inside ACE's sandbox**; by default an error blocks (on_error: block) — write warn explicitly to be lax.
plugins_hint: Drop plugins in .ace/plugins/<name>/: commands/*.md adds slash commands, hooks.json adds hooks. Plugins **cannot ship tools** in this version (that would mean running plugin code in-process).
plugins_footer: Plugin commands are prefixed with the plugin name (e.g. /myplugin:review) so they never collide with built-ins or other plugins.
hook_blocked_prompt: ⚠ A user_prompt hook blocked this input: {reason} (nothing was sent to the model)
cmd_todo: View/maintain the itemised todo list (add / start / done / remove / clear)
cmd_sessions: List recent sessions and pick one to continue
cmd_resume: Continue an existing session (index or filename)
cmd_fork: Start a new session seeded from an existing one
cmd_rewind: Rewind the conversation to after turn N (conversation only, not files)
todo_none: No todo store in this session.
todo_add_failed: not added (empty text, or the 50-item cap is reached)
sessions_pick: Pick a session to continue (Enter to confirm)
sessions_hint: Tip: /resume <index> continues · /fork [index] branches a new session · /rewind [turn] rewinds the conversation
rewind_files_hint: Note: rewind only touches the **conversation**. To restore files use /rollback (snapshots).
rewind_none: No conversation turns yet — nothing to rewind.
rewind_usage: Usage: /rewind [turn] ({turns} turns now; no argument drops the last turn)
cmd_review: Turn the last change into a patch, edit it in your editor, then read it back and apply
cmd_vim: Toggle vi editing mode / list custom keybindings
review_none: Nothing with a diff to review yet (have it change something first).
review_no_editor: No editor found (set ACE_EDITOR / VISUAL / EDITOR); the patch is at {path} for manual use.
review_opening: Opening editor: {editor} (save and quit to read it back)
review_unchanged: The patch is unchanged — nothing done.
review_apply_failed: Patch did not apply (no file was modified): {note}
review_applied: Applied back to {path} ({note}) — still through the execution layer (snapshot/permission/audit)
vim_on: vi mode: on (takes effect on the next prompt; Esc for normal mode, i/a to insert)
vim_off: vi mode: off (back to Emacs-style keys)
vim_hint: Custom keys go in the config's keybindings, e.g. {"c-e": "/expand"}; reserved keys (enter/esc/Ctrl+C) cannot be rebound.
at_image_usage: Usage: @image <path> (png/jpg/jpeg/webp/gif, max 4MB each, up to 3 images)
at_image_notice: Note: the image is **sent to the model provider as-is** (base64 in the request body). Check sensitive screenshots first.
at_image_help: @image attaches an image (multimodal input, sent to the model provider)
status_cost: Cost: {text} · in ≈{tin} / out ≈{tout} tokens (price table is a snapshot; override via config pricing)
cmd_stash: Stash / restore the current input (same as Ctrl+S)
cmd_queue: Queue a prompt to run right after this turn
keys_hint: To rebind, add to the config's keybindings (e.g. {"c-e": "/expand"}); reserved keys cannot be overridden.
keys_warn_reserved: {detail} is a safety key (Enter/Esc/Ctrl+C…) and cannot be overridden — ignored
keys_warn_app_bound: {detail} already has a real function (Ctrl+S/Ctrl+O/F1–F4…) — overriding would half-break both, so it was ignored
keys_warn_invalid: Invalid key name: {detail} (prompt_toolkit syntax, e.g. c-e / f5 / c-s-f)
keys_warn_not_cmd: Custom keys may only bind slash commands — ignored: {detail}
keys_warn_too_many: Too many custom keys ({detail}); only the first 20 are used
cmd_style: Output style presets: one preset drives both the prompt and how much the UI shows (/style [default|concise|explanatory|strict])
style_hint: /style <id> switches; a preset changes both the prompt sent to the model and how much the UI shows (an explicit /thinking toggle wins over the preset)
style_default_desc: No extra instruction; display is decided by the individual switches
style_concise_desc: Fewer words, no pleasantries; the UI keeps only the summary (no thinking, diffs capped at 40 lines)
style_explanatory_desc: One line of why before each action, plus trade-offs and pitfalls; the UI shows thinking and full cards
style_strict_desc: Report only what was verified: no "done" without a tool result, and say plainly when something could not be checked
cmd_term: Terminal capabilities (truecolor/alt screen/Unicode/mouse); /term check asks about the parts that cannot be probed
term_hint: /term check: are colours right, is Unicode clean, does the mouse work — autodetection cannot answer those, and you only find out it guessed wrong when the screen looks broken
term_probe_intro: Terminal capability self-check (Enter = default · b = back · Ctrl+C = cancel)
term_probe_saved: Recorded {n} probe answers (they override autodetection and are saved to the config)
cap_probe_color_ask: Do the boxes and text above have colour? (y/n)
cap_probe_unicode_ask: Do the glyphs render correctly (no boxes/question marks)? (y/n)
keys_enter: send (fills the selected completion first when the menu is open)
keys_search_history: reverse search history one entry at a time (cross-session)
keys_history_fuzzy: fuzzy-search history by keyword (dsk finds deepseek)
keys_expand: expand the last folded output / diff
keys_stash: stash the current input (/stash pop to restore)
keys_escape: quit on empty input; closes the completion menu first when open
keys_ctrl_c: clears input first; twice on an empty line quits
keys_bash: run a local command directly and paste its output into context (not via the model, still through the execution layer)
keys_help: a lone ? plus Enter shows this table
paste_folded: (paste folded into a placeholder: {n} lines; expanded automatically on submit)
bash_usage: Usage: !<command> (runs directly, through the execution layer; e.g. !git status)
bash_in_context: Output pasted into the conversation context.
stash_restored: Restored ({n} chars) into the prompt — press Enter to send.
queue_added: Queued ({n}); runs automatically after this turn.
queue_usage: Usage: /queue <text> (runs after the current turn) · /queue clear
